newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran reiterates claim over UAE disputed islands.
newsitem.headline: Iran reiterates claim over UAE disputed islands.

text.p: Iran on Sunday reiterated its ownership of the three Gulf islands at the centre of dispute with neighbouring United Arab Emirates (UAE) since 1992.
Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati termed "baseless" UAE claims on the islands of Abu Musa, Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb that are near key shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf.
"We shall save no efforts in defending our territorial sovereignty," the state-run radio quoted him as saying. Iran currently controls the islands.

"But our understanding is that UAE officials are willing to solve their problems in a friendly way. In that case, we welcome such suggestions," Velayati told reporters during a foreign ministry meeting on the Gulf region.
UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan earlier this month urged Iran to respond to an appeal for a peaceful solution to their row but said his country would continue to work to regain them.
Iran says its sovereignty over the islands is not negotiable and described a Gulf Arab summit stand earlier this year backing the UAE's claim as likely to increase tension in the region.
It has called for bilateral talks with the UAE to clear up any misunderstandings.
